claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your child(ren).

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm inquiring about one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here in the UK. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand the specific rules that apply. Let me read the official guidance first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details. I've reviewed the official eligibility rules. I can see that Alex is 17 and lives with you in the UK, which is helpful. However, I need to ask one more important question to determine your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

This is important because while Child Benefit normally stops at age 16, it can continue until age 20 if the child stays in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels. He's planning to finish those before deciding what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that! I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the official guidance I've reviewed:

- Alex is 17 years old and lives with you in the UK
- He is currently in approved education (A-levels at college)
- You are responsible for him and live with him

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. Importantly, the rules state: **"You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training."**

Since Alex is 17, lives with you, and is currently in approved education (A-levels), you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Your eligibility is based on the following:
- Alex is 17 years old (under 20)
- He is currently in approved education (A-levels)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for him

The rules specifically allow Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16 for children who remain in approved education or training. As long as Alex stays in approved education, you should continue to receive Child Benefit for him. If his circumstances change - for example, if he leaves college and doesn't go into other approved training - you would need to contact HMRC to update them.
